verdicts.reason: The text says that if the design file "is absent or empty: mark **Design Adherence** as not verified", and the check only applies when there is no design artifact.
The text says "If implementation changes cannot be identified, mark **Code Pattern Consistency** as not verified", and the check only applies when there are no repo edits.
The text gives a direct instruction: "Write the report to a file in the change directory: round 1 `/openspec/changes/issue/verify.md`".
The path "round 2 `/openspec/changes/issue/verify-2.md`" only matters if a second round happens, so requiring the file with no condition is stricter than written.
The required report format puts the rows "| Completeness |", "| Correctness |" and "| Coherence |" under "### Summary", so the check follows from the format.
The Summary rows follow from the format, but the check targets verify_2, which only exists "round 2", so applying it with no condition is stricter than written.
The text puts "Incomplete tasks" under "**CRITICAL** (Must fix before archive)".
The text calls for "Table for summary scorecard", so a markdown table in Summary follows directly.
"Code references in format: `file.ts:123`" sets the format for references when they appear, not a minimum number of them, so requiring at least one is stricter than written.
The text says "No vague suggestions like \"consider reviewing\"", which directly bans that phrase.
The text says "Create the proposal document that establishes WHY this change is needed."
The proposal template asks for "- **Why**: 1-2 sentences on the problem or opportunity."
The proposal template asks for "- **What Changes**: Bullet list of changes."
"What Changes" is described as a "Bullet list of changes", so a bullet item in that section follows.
The proposal template asks for "- **Capabilities**: Identify which specs will be created or modified".
"Identify which specs will be created or modified" means the capabilities have to be declared.
"Each becomes a new `specs/<capability-path>/spec.md`" directly ties each listed capability to a spec file.
The proposal template asks for "- **Modified Capabilities**: List existing capabilities whose REQUIREMENTS are changing."
The text says "Research existing specs before filling this in: run `openspec list --specs`", which matches running it before writing the proposal.
The text allows `--store` "only for a registered standalone store", so it is permitted in some cases, and banning it outright is stricter than written.
